parts.title: Campus Conversation: Joining a Student Club
script: Narrator
Listen to a conversation between a student and a member of the photography club.
Woman
Hi! Are you interested in the photography club?
Man
Yes, I am. I like taking pictures, but I am a beginner. Is that okay?
Woman
Of course. Many members are beginners. We meet every Thursday at six o'clock in the art building.
Man
Do I need a special camera?
Woman
No. You can use your phone. Some members use cameras, but it is not required.
Man
That is good. How much does it cost to join?
Woman
It is free, but there is one thing. Each member must show two photos at the end of the semester.
Man
Two photos? That sounds hard. But I think I can do it.
Woman
Don't worry. We help each other. Also, next week we are going to the park to take pictures of trees and flowers.
Man
That sounds fun. I want to go. How do I sign up?
Woman
Just write your name and email on this paper. Then we will send you a message.
Man
Okay. Here you go. Thank you for your help.
Woman
You're welcome. See you on Thursday!

questions.q: What is the conversation mainly about?
questions.exp: The student asks about joining the photography club.
She says they meet every Thursday at six o'clock.

questions.q: What does the student need to join?
o: Nothing special; a phone is fine
questions.exp: She says he can use his phone, and it is free.

questions.q: Listen again: "Don't worry. We help each other." Why does the woman say this?
o: To make the student feel better
To say the club is full
To ask the student to leave
questions.exp: The student is worried about showing two photos, so she comforts him.

questions.q: How does the student feel about the club at the end?
o: He is interested and wants to join
He is angry about the cost
He thinks the club is too far
questions.exp: He says it sounds fun and signs up.

questions.q: Where is the club going next week?
questions.exp: They are going to the park to take pictures of trees and flowers.

parts.title: Academic Lecture: How Do Plants Make Food?
script: Narrator
Listen to part of a lecture in a biology class.
Professor
Today we will talk about how plants make food. Animals eat other living things. But plants do not eat. They make their own food.
Professor
Plants make food with a process called photosynthesis. Plants need three things for photosynthesis: sunlight, water, and carbon dioxide.
Professor
First, the roots take water from the soil. The water moves up through the stem to the leaves.
Professor
Second, the leaves take in carbon dioxide from the air. Carbon dioxide is a gas. It goes into the leaf through very small holes.
Professor
Third, the leaves catch sunlight. Leaves are green because they have a green material called chlorophyll. Chlorophyll uses the energy from sunlight.
Professor
With this energy, the plant changes water and carbon dioxide into sugar. The sugar is the plant's food. The plant uses it to grow.
Professor
There is also something important for us. During photosynthesis, the plant makes oxygen and sends it into the air. People and animals need this oxygen to breathe.
Professor
So, plants help us in two ways. They are food for many animals, and they give us oxygen. For next class, please read about how plants grow from seeds.

questions.q: What is the lecture mainly about?
o: How plants make their own food

questions.q: What three things do plants need for photosynthesis?
questions.exp: She lists sunlight, water, and carbon dioxide.

o: They have a material called chlorophyll
questions.exp: Leaves have chlorophyll, which is green.

questions.q: Listen again: "The water moves up through the stem to the leaves." Why does the professor say this?
o: To show how water gets to the leaves
To describe the color of the stem
questions.exp: She explains the path of water from the roots to the leaves.

questions.q: What does the plant make from water and carbon dioxide?
questions.exp: The plant changes them into sugar, its food.

questions.q: How do plants help people and animals?
o: They give oxygen and are food for animals
questions.exp: The professor says plants are food and give oxygen.
